title: SparseLUT: Sparse Connectivity Optimization for Lookup Table-Based Deep Neural Networks
problem: Existing LUT-based DNN approaches (LogicNets, PolyLUT, NeuraLUT) rely on fixed sparsity masks determined by random seed optimization, which is inefficient and computationally expensive. SparseLUT addresses the need for deterministic, efficient connectivity optimization without requiring extensive random seed tuning.
motivation: LUT-based DNNs enable hardware-efficient inference on FPGAs and ASICs, but the dependency on random seed optimization in existing methods limits their optimization quality and practical scalability.
method: SparseLUT uses a connectivity-centric training technique with a non-greedy strategy that dynamically optimizes network structure during training. The method prioritizes pruning of less significant connections while strategically regrowing alternative ones, enabling efficient convergence to target sparsity. This approach operates without random seed optimization and incurs no additional hardware overhead.
key_novelty: Non-greedy connectivity-centric training that eliminates random seed optimization through dynamic pruning and strategic regrowth of connections in LUT-based DNNs.
contributions: Connectivity-centric training method for LUT-based DNNs that eliminates random seed optimization dependency
Non-greedy pruning and regrowth strategy enabling efficient convergence to target sparsity
Demonstrated accuracy improvements of up to 2.13% on MNIST and 0.94% on Jet Substructure Classification
State-of-the-art results for LUT-based DNNs without additional hardware overhead

metrics.accuracy: 2.13% improvement on MNIST, 0.94% improvement on Jet Substructure Classification
